LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 12.3.1 USE OF POSSESSIVES (MY, OUR, HER, HIS, THEIR, ITS)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.3: Language Use 12.3.1 Use of possessives (my, our, her, his, their, its)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 12.3.1 Use of possessives (my, our, her, his, their, its), part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Which words do we use to show ownership? 2. Why is it important to use possessives correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 12.3.1 Use of possessives (my, our, her, his, their, its) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn- learner develops relationships as they carry out an activity of showing assertiveness when referring to what belongs to

them with peers.

Values:
Responsibility: Accountability is developed as the learner endeavors to respect other people’s property when learning about possession.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self-awareness is nurtured as they learn self-awareness in relation to possession.
